Hi Dylan / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Orion is excited about the latency improvements from prefix caching. Procurement has one important clarification before we move to a pilot: when exactly do you bill for a cache 'hit'?

Our engineering team does a lot of short-turn prompts where a shared system prompt + small user suffix is common. Two scenarios that matter to us:
- If the system prompt and initial tokens are cache-resident and we only append a 12-token user message, do you charge for the full sequence or only the appended tokens?
- If we have session affinity and the model reuses cached KV across requests in the same session, is that considered a hit that avoids token billing for the prefix, or is there always a baseline charge per request?

Can you point to the exact line in the rate card or give a succinct example of how a 64-token system prompt + 12-token user message would be billed in both a cache-hit and cache-miss? Procurement flagged this as important for our cost model.

Attached is our draft SOW and a short example of request shapes.

Hi Laura — great questions, thanks for writing them up. Short answer up front: we charge only for tokens that traverse the full billing path (i.e., new decoding work), but there are a few edge cases teams trip over. Below I sketch the simple examples and then loop in Karthik from pricing for the exact rate-card wording.

Example (model with prefix caching enabled):
- Miss: system prompt (64t) + user (12t) = decoded from scratch => billed for 76 tokens.
- Hit (prefix cached & reused): cached prefix provides KV state for the 64-token system prompt, so only the 12 appended tokens are billed, assuming no re-encoding of the prefix is required.

Important caveats:
- If your request changes the system prompt text even slightly (character-level), it will be a cache miss. Cache keys are exact-match + normalization.
- Session affinity: if we reuse a warmed KV cache tied to a session, that behaves the same as an explicit prefix-hit; you will not be charged for prefix tokens. However, if the SDK or routing forces a re-compile or model variant fallback (e.g., quantized variant), some backend paths may bill more aggressively.
- Feature flags: some customers choose an "always-bill-minimum" setting for extremely low-latency requests to keep accounting simple; that's opt-in.

Lauren — can you confirm whether we can offer a short note in the SOW that clarifies the billing examples? Karthik, adding you for rate-card phrasing.

Thanks,
Dylan

Folks — quick rate-card language we can use. Please consider this the "authoritative snippet" for the hosted API in standard plans: 

"When a request is served from an exact-match prompt cache hit (including prefix cache and warmed KV cache), billing applies only to tokens that require new autoregressive decoding. Cached tokens that are restored from KV state are not billed. For multi-part requests, the billed token count equals the number of tokens generated or consumed beyond the cached prefix. Cache keys are canonicalized by trimming whitespace and normalizing UTF-8; any edit to the prefix invalidates the key."

Two clarifying examples we should include in the SOW: 
1) Full miss: client sends 64-token system + 12-token user -> billed tokens = 76.
2) Exact-match prefix hit: same 64-token system present in cache + 12-token user -> billed tokens = 12.

Notes: 
- If the request triggers a model variant fallback (we fallback from fp16 to an int8 variant due to capacity constraints), the fallback path may re-initialize and bill a higher baseline for the first request. We should call this out for customers with strict cost models.
- Enterprise customers can negotiate a 'prefix-free threshold' in the contract (e.g., first N warm prefixes per minute not billed) for high-volume shared-system work.

Hi Laura — looping in a short SOW paragraph and a small concession we can offer for the pilot. I'll paste the suggested wording below and then confirm the concession numbers.

Suggested SOW paragraph (for your SOW attachment):
"Redwood will apply prompt-state (prefix/KV) caching for eligible requests. For exact-match cache hits, billed tokens will include only the non-cached appended tokens. Cache keys are canonicalized; customers are responsible for stabilizing system prompts across requests if they wish to benefit from hits. In the event of model fallback or cache invalidation due to configuration changes, Redwood reserves the right to bill the first request after fallback as a full request."

Pilot concession: For the 90-day pilot, Redwood agrees to waive billing on prefix tokens for up to 10M prefix tokens per month. Any usage beyond that will be billed per the standard rate card. This concession is limited to requests routed to Redwood's hosted API in US regions.
